checked: The summary names the actual subject. The prose avoids the listed stock phrases and varies openings across explanation paragraphs and solutions.

The General Information layout follows Core Concept, Examples, and Traps. Example 1 uses six times monthly salary; Core Concept introduces the fine as up to six months’ salary. The multiplication expresses that already-taught ceiling. No other example uses a mathematical formula.

Examples 1–3 cover salary-based sanctions, denied process, and criminal sanctions; 4–6 cover principal, accomplice, and accessory acts; 7 applies disclosure conditions to disputed facts; 8 covers SALN misuse; 9–10 cover heavier penalties and independent removal.

Examples 11–14 cover CSC referral, reporter protection, review routing, and the escape-related accessory limitation. Each adds a distinct decision. The progression starts with basic ceilings and develops fact-based applications.
Every multi-step solution uses numbered steps. Example 1 displays its key multiplication. Examples 9 and 12 are one-step answers and need no numbered list. No intervening reasoning step is omitted.
The only display equation is 6 times 30,000 equals 180,000. It is short enough for a phone screen.
Body paragraphs contain one to three sentences. The explanation uses headings and short paragraphs rather than dense bullet lists.
